title: Review of c34's rod-recoil negative: replicates on fresh seed 9 (daughters move 3.1/5.0/7.1 px after 10/20/40 frames, 10.1 px over a life; kr=0 gives a worm network with 0 persistent splits), but at zeta 0.8 the speed by life decile is U-shaped, not a steady slowdown
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged (zeta 0.8, phi_b -0.6, kr 0.012) on fresh seed 9 (labkit, T=1000) with c34's motionphase.py, and with kr=0 on the same seed (T=1500). Default: 38 splits, 23 persistent, generation 4; 33 split-born tracks >= 40 frames move a median 3.1 / 5.0 / 7.1 px after 10 / 20 / 40 frames and 10.1 px over their whole life; mean step by life decile 0.303 0.287 0.254 0.219 0.203 0.211 0.219 0.253 0.287 0.290 px/frame (results.txt). kr=0: rods fuse into a branched active worm network (kr0/sheet.png), 893 splits, 0 persistent, 717 merges, occupancy 0.24.

observations.M: results.txt: whole-life net 10.1 px for split-born rods, far below 3 body lengths; first-decile step 0.30 px/frame
observations.D: kr0/sheet.png and FACTS: 0 persistent splits without the chemostat

seeds_run.result: pass for the distances and the kr=0 network; the post-fission slowdown at zeta 0.8 is U-shaped (0.30 -> 0.20 -> 0.29)

verdicts.limitation: At the default zeta 0.8 the step falls by a third over the first half of life and rises again before the next fission (also visible in c34's own zeta 0.8 row), so 'slows with age' holds only for the first half; the distance conclusion does not depend on it. The kr=0 run shows fine stripes in the s and order channels after t~1300 (kr0/sheet.png), which may be a numerical artifact of the dense network. The finding's kr=0 command line, like other packs, does not record its WORLD_P.
